leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members place B040 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) in their preferred round-1 configuration, and Eriksson and Mehlig list it as their first or second alternative. Shared: the magic-wavelength scheme, reproduction and intercomparison at the 1e-18 level across several national laboratories, and a compact two-name credit. Not shared: whether the pair is a stand-alone prize (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce) or one half of a two-part prize with B028 (Danielsson, Olsson); and how much weight to give the 2005 and 2012 precedents, the pending redefinition of the second, and contributors outside the pair. Several of these six moved to B040 only after reading the opening ballots, so the number partly reflects convergence and not independent first choices.

Two members pair the lattice clock with Hosono's discovery of iron-based superconductors (three laureates in total). They agree that the two parts are separate, mature, cleanly credited achievements, and that Hosono's case rests on discovery and not on explaining the pairing mechanism. They also concede that the pairing has no common thread. B028 has no other explicit supporter in a preferred configuration; Eriksson lists it as an alternative. Open points are the unexplained mechanism, the early Tc increases by other groups, and whether a single-person part is enough.

Two members prefer B061 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect) as a stand-alone prize on a theory-plus-experiment footing, and both rate it as conceptually original and independently confirmed over about two decades. Both name the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (and the 3D pioneers) as the main weakness, and they differ from other members on whether the 2016 topological-phases prize is partial overlap or duplication. Mehlig explicitly treats B040 as the better-attributed fallback if the credit cannot be drawn cleanly. B061 is an alternative for Johansson, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce.

areas_of_agreement: B040 is the only shortlisted candidate that every member ranked at opening, and six of eight now include it in their preferred round-1 configuration; none argues that the physics is unsound or the result unreproduced.

Several members rely on the same evidence for B040: independent intercomparison at the 1e-18 level across JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, SYRTE, PTB, NIST and NPL, plus tests of constants, millimetre-scale redshift and dark-matter searches.

Members agree that attribution quality matters as much as scientific merit: IceCube, B017 and B055 were all lowered or set aside by their own advocates because of credit problems (collaboration size and precursors, crowded priority, absent architects).
Members accept the three-laureate limit and the discovery-or-invention-plus-verification standard. Both B040 and B061 are regarded as mature and not premature.

Five members say they changed position after reading the opening ballots (Danielsson toward B040, Johansson from B055 to B040, Mehlig from B008 to B061, Olsson from B046 to B040 plus B028, Pearce from B018 to B040), so first-round positions are provisional.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a discovery or invention in physics (a new regime of many-body quantum control, relativistic geodesy, constants and dark-matter tests) or an instrument advance within already honoured precision measurement. Eriksson, Danielsson and Olsson raise this, while Kroll, Lindroth and Johansson answer with the many-body and redshift results.

Whether the iron-based superconductors (B028) justify a prize while the pairing mechanism remains unexplained, and whether the discovery should be credited as a family of materials and not as the Tc record.

Whether B061 is a new class of matter beyond what the 2016 prize recognised (time-reversal-invariant Z2 class versus Chern and phase-transition topology), as Eriksson and Mehlig argue, or overlap, as Olsson and Danielsson read it.

Whether topological insulators and active-matter flocking (B008) have the quantitative experimental confirmation needed; Eriksson notes the Toner-Tu exponents are not cleanly confirmed, and Mehlig did not resolve this.
attribution_disputes: B040: whether Katori (concept and first lattice clock) and Ye (record accuracy and many-body clocks) suffice, or whether Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom, Lemonde, Gill or Takamoto have a claim of comparable weight. Several members say they have not verified early Tokyo and JILA priority.

B061: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe as the host and are not credited; Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents and Roy lie partly outside the slate. Eriksson holds that a citation built on the prediction and the observation can handle this, while Olsson, Danielsson and Mehlig regard it as contestable.

B017 and B055: B017 has several near-simultaneous 1991 demonstrations with Chu outside the slate; B055 omits Girvin. B018 (two names for a very large collaboration with AMANDA and DUMAND precursors) and B046 (Krivanek outside Rose, Haider and Urban) have comparable gaps. These matter chiefly as alternatives and fallbacks.
B028: Kamihara and the early Chinese Tc work are not in the single-name credit of Hosono, which affects citation wording.
maturity_disputes: The redefinition of the second has not yet been adopted; members differ on whether that makes B040 prospective or whether it is a procedural matter that does not bear on whether the physics works.

Precedent timing: 2005 (comb) and 2012 (ion control) for B040, 2016 for B061, and the 2025 circuit prize for B055. Members disagree on whether proximity to a recent prize counts as overlap or as natural continuation.

Eighteen years after discovery, B028 is mature by age. Danielsson lists the unresolved pairing mechanism among his own reservations but, answering Olsson, says it is no reason to wait; Olsson also records it as a reservation. Whether it argues for waiting is not settled.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs WACQT and is close to the circuit QED community; she states she should recuse from deciding B055 and has moved it to an alternative.

Kroll spent part of his PhD in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder (Hall shared the 2005 prize), and Jun Ye is a JILA colleague of that tradition; he reports no direct collaboration or institutional tie to Katori or Ye. He also leads part of WACQT, relevant to B055 and not to B040.
Olsson is an electron microscopist at Chalmers and B046 is in her own field; she has not made it her preferred part, and she notes Johansson is also at Chalmers Physics.

Lindroth is a theorist in the same broad AMO precision-measurement community as B040, a long-time collaborator of the 2023 laureate L'Huillier (not a candidate), and asks for a colleague from outside AMO to test the case.
Danielsson is closest to B023 in field and says this is a reason to weigh his own ranking there lightly.

Eriksson chaired the 2025 committee that awarded the circuit tunnelling prize, relevant to B055 but not a personal conflict. Mehlig has subject proximity to B008 only. Pearce (chair) works in astroparticle physics adjacent to IceCube (B018), his first alternative, and has no recorded tie to the clock groups or to IceCube.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee state in one sentence why the optical lattice clock is a distinct invention, and not an increment on the 2005 frequency comb and the 2012 ion-control prizes, and does it count as physics discovery or as instrumentation? Kroll and Lindroth are asked to offer draft citation wording.

Is two names (Katori, Ye) defensible against Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom, Lemonde, Gill and Takamoto, and what do the external expert reports say about early Tokyo versus JILA priority? Does anyone argue for a third laureate within the three-name limit?

Should B040 stand alone (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce), or be paired with B028 (Danielsson, Olsson)? What pairing or sole-prize rationale would the committee defend, and is a prize with no common thread acceptable?

For B028, does an unexplained pairing mechanism and the early Tc increases by other groups argue for waiting, and can the citation credit the discovery of the family to Hosono alone without implying a Tc record?

For B061, can the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and 3D-pioneer credit gap be handled by citation wording (Eriksson's position), or does it disqualify the three-name allocation (Olsson, Danielsson)? Does the 2016 prize amount to overlap, and is Mehlig willing to fall back to B040 if the gap is not resolved?

Do the members who rank B040 low or mid (Eriksson, Danielsson, Johansson at opening) object on scientific grounds, or only from distance to the field? What would each need to see to support it in the final ballot?

Should the alternatives that were set aside for attribution reasons (B018, B017, B055, B046) and the one-supporter candidates (B023, B008) be formally dropped, or does any member intend to revive them with a credit fix?
summary.chair_observation: Round-1 positions are clustered but not settled. B040 appears in six of eight preferred configurations (four stand-alone, two paired with B028), B061 is the preferred stand-alone choice of two members, and no other ballot is preferred by anyone. The leading position is the product of several members revising their opening ballots after reading each other, so it should be tested and not treated as a count of independent first choices. The principal open issues are the lattice clock's overlap with earlier metrology prizes and the two-name credit, whether a second part (B028) is wanted, and whether the B061 credit gap can be repaired by citation wording. Nothing here is a ruling, and every figure above is counted only from positions explicit in the eight round-1 files.
